name: British Arts and Crafts

description.short: The reform movement that rejected industrial ornament in favour of honest material, visible craft, and the dignity of the vernacular cottage.
description.long:
Morris, Webb, Voysey, Lethaby, and Lutyens argued that the machine had corrupted both the object and the person who made it, and that architecture should return to local material, direct construction, and the modest forms of the rural cottage. The argument was moral before it was aesthetic.

It is the most philosophically explicit family in the taxonomy, and the one whose ideas travelled furthest — to Stickley's Craftsman in America, to the Deutscher Werkbund, and by an unexpected route into modernism, which kept the honesty-of-material argument while discarding the craft.

defining_characteristics: Material honesty: construction expressed rather than concealed
Local and traditional materials preferred to industrial substitutes
The vernacular cottage taken seriously as a model for serious architecture
Ornament arising from craft process rather than applied from a catalog
An explicit moral argument connecting how things are made to how people live
